name: 👑 Orontes III
party: year-level backbone — first Orontid king of the era; preceded by the satrap Mihran (321–317 BC) after Alexander's empire fragmented; dates approximate

name: 👑 Arsames I
party: year-level backbone — ruled Armenia, Sophene and Commagene; Sames held Armenia and Sophene c. 260 BC

name: 👑 Orontes IV
party: year-level backbone — last Orontid king of Armenia; Xerxes ruled Sophene/Commagene concurrently 228–212 BC

name: 👑 Artaxias I
party: year-level backbone — gap 200–190 BC (Seleucid control; Artaxias as satrap); founded the Artaxiad dynasty, king from c. 190 BC after Rome broke Seleucid power at Magnesia

name: 👑 Tigranes II the Great
party: year-level backbone — gap 159–95 BC (Artavasdes I, Tigranes I — dates unattested in source); empire at its greatest extent, 'King of Kings'

name: 👑 Artavasdes II
party: year-level backbone — captured by Mark Antony, 34 BC

name: 👑 Artaxias II
party: year-level backbone — c. dates; gap 34–30 BC (Roman/Parthian interregnum)

name: 👑 Tigranes IV and Erato
party: year-level backbone — co-rule; Erato reigned alone 1–2 AD

name: 👑 Tigranes V and Erato
party: year-level backbone — c. dates; last Artaxiads — dynasty ended 12 AD; gap 2–6 AD (Roman appointees)

name: 👑 Tiridates I
party: year-level backbone — founder of the Arsacid line; first reign 52–58, restored 62, crowned by Nero in Rome in 66; reign interrupted 58–62

name: 👑 Tiridates III
party: year-level backbone — gap 88–298 (intervening Arsacid kings only partially attested at year level); made Christianity Armenia's state religion, traditionally in 301 — first Christian state

name: 👑 Arshak II
party: year-level backbone — gap 330–350 (Khosrov III, Tiran); caught between Rome and Sasanian Persia

name: 👑 Pap
party: year-level backbone — assassinated at Roman instigation

name: 👑 Vramshapuh
party: year-level backbone — gap 374–389 (Varazdat, Arshak III/Khosrov IV); under him Mesrop Mashtots devised the Armenian alphabet

name: 👑 Artaxias IV
party: year-level backbone — gap 414–422 (Shapur, then direct Sasanian rule 417–422); deposed by Bahram V of Persia in 428 — monarchy abolished, Armenia placed under marzbans
